prompt_translate_this_full_text.message:
Translate the email below into {%thunderai_translate_lang%}.

Rules:
- Translate both the subject and the body.
- Return the result as a JSON object with three fields: "subject", "body" and "status".
- If the translation has been done the status is equal to 1.
- If the email is written in one of these languages "{%thunderai_translate_exclude_lang%}" or in the {%thunderai_translate_lang%} language, return an empty string for the body and the subject and set the status to -1.
- Do not add explanations, notes, or any text outside the JSON.

Mail subject: {%mail_subject%}

Mail body: {%mail_html_body%}

Generate a response in JSON format only. The output should be only a JSON object. Here is an example of the JSON format to be used:
{
"subject": "subject translation",
"body": "body translation",
"status": "status result"
}

prompt_get_calendar_event_full_text.message:
Extract all relevant details required to generate a calendar event from the following text. The extracted information should include:
- Event Title
- Start Date and Time (including timezone, if specified)
- End Date and Time (including timezone, if specified)
- Full day (if mentioned)
- Attendees
Ensure the data is formatted clearly and consistently so that it can be directly used for creating a calendar event.
If there are relative time references, consider that the date and time of the email are "{%mail_datetime%}". Calculate the start date and time based on this reference. If the calculated start date and time are earlier than "{%current_datetime%}", recalculate the start date and time using "{%current_datetime%}" as the base.
If the duration is not specified, set it to one hour.
These are the attendees: {%author%}, {%recipients%}, {%cc_list%}. If present, exclude my address: {%account_email_address%}.
If the event is a full day event, endDate must be one day after startDate with time set to "T000000".
If you're not able to get one or more of the required information, please respond with an empty string.
Generate a response in JSON format only. Do not include any additional text or explanations; provide only the JSON. Here is the format to be used:
{
"startDate": "YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS",
"endDate": "YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS",
"summary": "Calendar event summary here",
"forceAllDay": false,
"attendees": [attendee1@example.com,attendee2@example.com,attendee3@example.com]
}
Here's the text:"{%mail_text_body_or_selected%}"

prompt_spamfilter_full_text.message:
Analyze the following email and determine if it is spam or not. Consider factors such as suspicious keywords, excessive promotional language, misleading subject lines, requests for personal information, and unusual sender addresses.
Provide a value from 0 (not spam) to 100 (spam) and an explanation of no more than 10 words.
In case of missing message data, set the value to 0 (not spam), and give the reason.
Generate a response in JSON format only. Do not include any additional text or explanation; provide only the JSON. Here is the format to be used:
{
"explanation": "Brief explanation of your reasoning",
"spamValue": <integer from 0 to 100>
}
Here there are the mail information:
Sender: "{%author%}"
Subject: "{%mail_subject%}"
Html body: "{%mail_html_body%}"

prompt_inbox_triage_full_text.message: You are an expert email assistant who helps the user keep a clean, well organized inbox. Classify each email below into exactly one of the given categories, using the category descriptions. Prefer the most specific category, and prefer the user's own custom categories when they match. An email only "needs reply" when a real person is personally waiting for an answer from the user; automated, bulk and marketing emails never need a reply. Mark as high priority only what is time sensitive or clearly important for the user. Be careful with spam: use it only for obvious junk, scams or phishing.
prompt_inbox_triage_full_text.description: Default instructions of the Inbox Assistant sorting prompt

prompt_inbox_brief_full_text.message: You are the user's email assistant. Using the list of emails below, write a short briefing of what needs the user's attention. Use these sections when they apply: Reply needed, To do (with deadlines), Important information. Keep each point to one line, start with the most urgent, reference emails as [n] and finish with one line about what can be safely ignored.
prompt_inbox_brief_full_text.description: Instructions of the Inbox Assistant brief prompt

prompt_inbox_reply_full_text.message: Write a reply to the email below on behalf of the user. Be clear, friendly and concise, answer every question that was asked, and do not invent facts: if information is missing, leave a short placeholder in square brackets. Output only the body of the reply, without subject line and without quoting the original email.
prompt_inbox_reply_full_text.description: Instructions of the Inbox Assistant reply prompt

prompt_inbox_followup_full_text.message: The user sent the emails below and did not receive an answer yet. For each email decide if it expects an answer (a question, a request, a proposal, a pending decision). Thank-you notes, confirmations, FYI messages and automatic replies do not expect an answer. Give a one-line summary of what the user is waiting for.
prompt_inbox_followup_full_text.description: Instructions of the Inbox Assistant follow-up prompt
